To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Next, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These values of x are the critical points of the function. To determine if these critical points are stationary points, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x). If the second derivative is positive at a critical point, the function has a local minimum at that point. If the second derivative is negative, the function has a local maximum at that point. If the second derivative is zero, the test is inconclusive.
